In the hell realms, among animals, hungry ghosts <note>original: "yi-dvags"</note>, the demigod realm, and among human beings, there appears to be much suffering. The pure lands of the Buddhas are for the most part not like this. These are also times of decline.

Due to the intermediate aeon of famine, the unbearable suffering of famine occurs in the world from time to time. Due to the intermediate aeon of sickness, many diseases arise. Due to the intermediate aeon of weapons, there arises much mutual harm. Due to the destruction by water, the aspects of desire <note>original: "nyon-mongs" or kleshas, here interpreted as defilements</note> become dominant in existence; due to destruction by fire, the aspects of hatred become dominant; and due to destruction by wind, the aspects of ignorance become dominant, and so forth, leading to many faults of the times.

Regarding the decline of lifespan, the lives of sentient beings have no certainty. At times, the measure of lifespan is immeasurable. At other times, it becomes a lifespan of ten years. That too is uncertain; some die while still in the womb. Some die as soon as they are born, or during childhood, or during youth, or in the prime of life, or when they reach maturity, or when they are halfway through their lifespan, or in old age, and so on; there is no certainty in death. Because of this, there is much grief, lamentation, suffering, and mental unhappiness present in the world.

Regarding the decline of views, there are sixty-two types of extremely harmful views that destroy all virtue, when divided specifically. Those who have firmly entered into wrong views cannot be cured even by a thousand Buddhas. Moreover, all non-Buddhist sectarians are characterized by disparagement, lack of faith, failure to assemble, and are extremely disparaged. They are by nature not fit vessels, their mental continuums having become for the most part like pungent spices, or for the most part like garlic, unable to be reached by the holy Dharma in their minds.

Homage to the youthful <term>Manjushri</term>.

Why was this sutra, which states, "A <term>bodhisattva</term> <gloss>enlightenment-being</gloss>, a great being, should not abandon these four dharmas even for the sake of their own life as long as they live," composed? It was composed to provide correct instruction to those confused about the methods for attaining supreme enlightenment for those who have entered the Great Vehicle <term>Mahayana</term>, to ensure those who are heedless correctly uphold these practices, to encourage those who are discouraged, and to bring joy to those who have already correctly entered the path.

The mention of the number four is intended to avoid fear of an expansive subject and to prevent those who might not wish to hear it from turning away. By stating a number, it is easily remembered. Below, patience and humility are mentioned, but since they serve the same purpose, they are not distinct.

Although there are many categories for those who have entered the Great Vehicle, two names are used for three reasons: through aspiration, through application, and through realization. What is meant by aspiration? They are called <term>bodhisattva</term> <gloss>enlightenment-being</gloss> because they aspire to profound knowledge, and they are called a <term>mahasattva</term> <gloss>great being</gloss> because they aspire to great power. What is meant by application? It is because they exert themselves for the sake of their own supreme, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and because they work to save all sentient beings from suffering. What is meant by realization? It is because enlightenment is realized through two powers. What are the two? They are the power of wisdom and the power of diligence. <margin>The end of Alchemy is not gold and silver, but secrets.</margin>

<margin>Poison exists even in the best things.</margin>
Who is there who would dare to deny that poison lies and exists even in the best things? Everyone is forced to admit this. If this is true, then I ask you: should not the poison be separated from the good and useful? And should the good not be accepted, and the evil left behind? Indeed, it must be so. If it must be so, then I ask you to explain to me how it is separated in your shops. For with you, everything remains mixed. But to defend your own simplicity, if you are convicted to admit that poison lies therein and are asked where it finally goes, you then bring up some nonsense about "corrections" which supposedly extract and remove the poison,
<margin>The correction of physicians is ventilated.</margin>
just as they correct Quince with Scammony, or later with Diagridium. But what kind of correction is that? Does the poison not remain afterwards just as it was at first? And yet, you meanwhile boast that you have corrected it, so that the poison no longer harms. But where has it escaped to? 
<margin>Diagridium.</margin>
It remains in the Diagridium. Test that, if you are wise: exceed the measure, and you will see where the poison is. For you will know it quite quickly. Thus you also correct Turbith, and call it Diaturbith. These are your kinds of corrections, which would befit rustics and should be fed to horses. Make a test by exceeding the measure, and increase the dose: you will see if you do not feel the poison. 
<margin>What a "corrective" physician is.</margin>
*To correct is to take the corrected.* Whoever is malicious and has sinned, if he is punished, the correction does not extend further than the will of the one who has been punished lasts. Such are these corrections, too; it depends on them, not on you. Now, in this case, the physician has nothing more to consider than that the poison be taken away. This must be done through separation: as, for example, a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted into food. If you take the poison out of it, you may eat it with no harm. The same must be understood regarding all other things; namely, that there is a need for a similar separation. That not having been done, you cannot be secure in your operation, unless it happens that nature makes up for your shortcomings, or the greater benevolence of the heavens favors you. For in your art, no protection will remain.

Now, therefore, if that true foundation is needed which removes the poison, how does Alchemy achieve it? For it must be done in such a way that if Mars <note>alchemical term for iron</note> is in the Sun <note>alchemical term for gold</note>, the Mars is removed, and if Saturn <note>alchemical term for lead</note> is in Venus <note>alchemical term for copper</note>, it is separated from it. For as many as the ascendants and impressions in the things of nature are, so many bodies exist within them. But as for those bodies which are contrary, it is necessary that some part of them be removed and taken away, so that by this means all contrariety may be lifted, and the evil which you seek may be taken from the good.
<margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin>
As gold is useful for nothing unless it is first cast into the fire, so much less useful is medicine that does not pass through the fire. For it is necessary that all things pass through fire into a second generation, which ought to conduct and assist man. And should this not deservedly be considered the approved foundation of any physician? For the physician ought not to employ poisons, but true secrets <term>arcana</term>. 
<margin>The shops are reproved.</margin>
But all those shop-preparations, however many there are, do not contribute even a letter to this doctrine. Rather, they are simply occupied in "correcting," just as if a dog were to fart in a room, and that stench were to be suppressed either by troches and incense, or by juniper wood. I ask you: does the stench not remain in the room afterwards just as it was before? And although it might not be perceived by smell, is one therefore allowed to say that the stench has been separated and remains no longer? No, it is present, but corrected by the smoke. Thus, the smoke and the stench enter the nostrils together. Such also are the corrections of the apothecaries, who dull an "Allopathic" <note>likely referring to a harsh medicine</note> with sugar, so that it might inflict no harm. Thus, sugar and honey are their masteries. Thus, they also correct Gentian with Theriac. But are these not works of asinine ignorance? Yet they boast and sell themselves as the chief of physicians. But who is so stupid as not to smell immediately that these things are worthless? ## CHAPTER II.

**T**here is, therefore, in all metals a true Mercury and a right sulfur, equally in imperfect as in perfect metals; it is only that it has been made contaminated and impure in imperfect metals, which are the only ones deprived of perfect maturation. And for the same reasons, they can be reduced to gold and silver; that is, the impurity with which they were defiled may be separated from the golden or silver nature that is in them, and the form of gold or silver be instilled into them. For they have been torn away from nature because they were removed and dug up from natural passages, mines, and veins of the earth; therefore, they can no longer have any operation in themselves as if they were still hiding underground; nevertheless, as much as lies within them, they desire to be perfected.
